newsitem.title: FRANCE: French immigration bill prompts new Paris march.
newsitem.headline: French immigration bill prompts new Paris march.

text.p: Several thousand demonstrators marched through Paris on Sunday to demand that the centre-right government withdraw a controversial immigration bill intended to shut loopholes in already tough existing laws.

Leftist movements, including the Socialist and Communist parties, backed the march called by anti-racism groups, trade unions and intellectuals ahead of a final reading debate in the Senate on Tuesday.

"We are here to sound the alarm bell once again," Mouloud Aounit, of the anti-racism MRAP movement, said after the bill's passage through the National Assembly last month prompted protests from film-makers and artists.
The bill aims to close loopholes in tough existing laws dating from 1933 and would grant the police extended powers to track immigrants in France, and set up records of visitors staying in France.
One key article authorises police to keep the passports or travel documents of illegal immigrants and allows searches of commercial vehicles within 20 km (12 miles) of the border.
It also authorises police to take the fingerprints of foreigners from outside the European Union who apply for a residence permit.
"Immigration is not the country's chief problem," said writer Dan Franck. "The authorities should do their job rather than designate scapegoats."

Franck was among hundreds of artists, lawyers and writers who signed petitions urging the French to disobey the bill if it becomes law in a rebellion against a provision that citizens should report to authorities the departure of foreign guests.
The bill has been amended to order guests themselves to notify authorities of their departure.
